Thirty-one comments

The Steampacket

Zina sent me an email asking for my “setting” of this tune, too grand a word for how I play it, which is not far off the standard session settings I’ve heard from other fiddlers.

I originally learned that opening bar of the first half as: |A~G3 AGFD| and I still use that on occasion, but to me it lacks punch. Sometimes I play that first measure as: |DGBG AGFG| and sometimes I like to repeat the AGFG in the following measure for a little swing:

|(3GGG BG AGFG|AGFG Addc|

My B part is even closer to the “standard” version…I roll almost all those high g’s, tho I suppose with a little noodling I could come up with something more creative. At session speed, though, I like the way the rolls ring out, so there they are. :-)

Incidentally, the Steampack makes a nice follow-up to Bantry Lasses, which I posted not too long ago.

↳ Posted by Will Harmon on May 20th, 2002.

Oops

In the second to last measure, that should be an f after the triplet: |af (3gfe fde^c| d2 etc.

I fixed it in the abc notation. Gawd, if the clients I edit for saw what havoc I wreak in here….

This tune packs a mean, powerful piston rod action!

It takes its name from the famous shipping company that was founded in London in 1839 by Scotland’s own James MacQueen http://www.merchantnavyofficers.com/rm1.html The state sponsored company would become the largest shipping group in the world a hundred years on.
See also: http://www.steam-packet.com/ for the Hiberno-Manx connections (so to say!)

The Steampacket, X:12

Paddy Canny’s version, as linked in my previous comment - some interesting and piquant touches. As seems standard with Canny, there are some quite in-between/sliding pitches; that top B sounds pretty flat and so I’ve transcribed it as such, but it doesn’t feel straightforward, and some of the high F-naturals are somewhat sharp. Little point trying to show that in notation though, when one can hear the recording instead!
*** I said in my previous comment that it’s in the dorian mode but I think I was fixating on that high B[flat] a bit, and mixolydian seems closer to the truth.
